# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 29 (Bu-Vb Np29)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np29
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 29
**Title (English, from literature):** Storing a robe for more than six days in an inhabited area
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 29, titled *Sāsaṅka*, is an ecclesiastical rule belonging to the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule provides that a monk who stores any of his three robes in an inhabited area for more than six days incurs an offense of expiation involving forfeiture (*nissaggiya pācittiya*), obliging him to relinquish the robe and confess the transgression. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
